item.title: Top 10 hiking destinations to visit on your sailing charter
item.description: When you think about hiring a yacht, you might see yourself lounging on the deck or swimming in turquoise waters. But to truly experience the essence of a new destination, you won’t regret stepping ashore for a hike – the perfect activity for any sailing itinerary. Like sailing, hiking allows you to access exclusive places and incredible views away from the hustle and bustle of tourist traps. Ready to drop your anchor and explore? Keep reading for a rundown of the top 10 hiking destinations you can visit from Dream Yacht Charter’s 35 locations. 1. Corsica, France If you can’t choose between sweeping mountains or a coastal paradise, hiking in Corsica is for you. The island offers hikers an incredible combination of both terrains, many within easy reach of Dream Yacht’s Ajaccio marina base. The island is home to Europe’s most challenging trail (the famous GR20), but it also features a diverse array of paths suitable for more casual day hikers. The La Cascade géante de la Piscia Di Gallu loop takes you through fragrant local vegetation, ending at a spectacular 70-metre waterfall. It takes just 90 minutes, making it perfect for a morning hike before returning to your yacht! More adventurous trekkers will love the panoramic Bocca di Cuccavera trail , a 3.5-hour climb with stunning views of the Mediterranean and Corsica’s rugged interior. The sailing season runs from May through October, with spring and autumn offering ideal hiking temperatures and fewer crowds on the trails. 2. Martinique, Caribbean Are you dreaming of hiking through a rainforest paradise? Martinique’s volcanic terrain features tropical trails that feel straight out of a storybook! The island makes hiking easy with well-marked trails and accessible anchorages near Le Marin, Dream Yacht’s Martinique base. The 4.5-hour Sainte-Anne to Baie des Anglais loop offers one of the island’s most rewarding coastal hikes, taking you through pristine beaches, mangrove forests, and dramatic cliff paths – all with the turquoise Caribbean constantly at your side. Moor in Sainte-Anne’s protected bay, Grande Anse d’Arlet’s picturesque cove, or Saint-Pierre’s historic harbour. With dryer conditions and clear views, December through April are ideal for hiking in Martinique. 3. French Polynesia, South Pacific From coastal tropical forests to cloud-shrouded mountain peaks, hiking the Society Islands of French Polynesia is unlike anything else in the Pacific islands. With dramatic volcanic terrain, the island’s significant elevation gain offers hikers an array of ecosystems to explore in a single outing. From Dream Yacht’s Raiatea base, the Tapioi Trail provides a perfect introduction to Polynesian hiking. It features a relatively easy ascent through lush rainforest, leading to spectacular views of Raiatea’s lagoon and neighbouring islands. For a more immersive (and advanced) experience, the Three Waterfalls Trail takes you deep into Raiatea’s jungle interior, where cascading natural pools provide refreshing swimming stops along your route. Drive to the trail head from our base in Uturoa on Raiatea to gain access to these remarkable trails. For dry trails and crystal-clear visibility, plan your yacht charter between May and October. 4. Corfu, Greece Since the time of the ancient Greeks, Corfu’s extensive network of footpaths has enchanted visitors. The island offers over 220km of marked trails through olive groves, coastal cliffs, and mountain viewpoints with unforgettable views of the Ionian Sea. From Dream Yacht Charter’s Gouvia Marina base in Corfu , you can reach famous trails like the Gouviá to Liapádes route . This adventure takes you through traditional villages and rustic landscapes before descending to one of Corfu’s most beautiful beaches—perfect for a post-hike swim! If you love history, the historic Monastery Vlacherna-Achilleion path combines cultural heritage with natural beauty. item.title: NEW! Electric concept cruiser available for BVI charters
item.description: A new way of boating The Beneteau brand’s boat building legacy dates back to 1884 when Benjamin Beneteau founded the BENETEAU boatyard in France, later producing the region’s first engine-powered fishing boat in 1909. Today, Beneteau yachts remain one of the largest and most respected brands in the industry with continued innovations in terms of both boats of processes. It’s no surprise that they continue to challenge boundaries with a new reimagined hybrid electric “monohull”. A modern alternative to charter monohull & catamaran sailing Their latest venture follows extensive research dedicated to listening to the voices of countless charter guests, and collecting invaluable data about their real-world experiences. The result is the exciting new electric Island Cruising Concept designed specifically for idyllic charter holidays on the water. Step aboard this new concept boat and experience cruising at a peaceful pace, similar to a sailboat, but without the hassle of sail handling. Enjoy freedom and autonomy with hybrid electric technology, along with spacious living areas similar to a catamaran and comfortable accommodations for up to 8 guests. Sustainability meets cruising pleasure With an eye toward eco-conscious cruising combined with superior onboard comfort, Beneteau has engineered the Island Cruising Concept to operate for extended periods under full electric, emissions-free power – the ultimate choice for eco-conscious boating enthusiasts. Around 30 to 50% of the boat’s energy requirement is achieved through the power of the sun, with large roof-mounted solar panels. Charterers can enjoy easy cruising from one island to the next with a full electric range of more than 2.5 hours at 7kts. The boat’s software system ensures stress-free energy management. And, of course, a propulsion back-up is provided with the generator providing a range of nearly 250NM at 7kts. Take your charter vacation to the next level with a boat that’s respectful to the environment, and also more enjoyable with the complete absence of noise – just peaceful, silent operation – similar to sailing but with less effort! You can even make your vacation budget go further with exceptional savings through fuel efficiency. It’s also worth noting that this boat recently won an award as the Eco-Focused Launch of the Year (Over 10m LOA category), at the IBI METS Trade/Boatbuilder Awards 2024 . Indoor & outdoor living spaces blend seamlessly The main living space aboard the Island Cruising Concept is covered for protection from the elements, while providing an open-air experience that’s wide open on all sides for fresh breezes, expansive views and an unparalleled feeling of oneness with nature and the sea. This covered living space is light and bright, with 360 views and houses an outdoor kitchen, dining table, and bench lounging seat, as well as a comfortable helm station. Platforms at the back and foldout terraces on either side further expand the space and open feel, while providing easy access to the water for swimming and water sports. Doorways on either side of the covered living area allow easy access to the lounging areas on the bow. Here, guests can sunbathe or take in the stars at night from the comfortable padded bench seating and sunbed lounge areas that rival the space on the bow of a catamaran. When ready to retire for the evening, tuck below to discover four comfortable guest cabins with ensuite baths, plus a single forepeak crew cabin. Superior design for ultimate chartering comfort Comfort and efficiency aboard the Island Cruising Concept is further enhanced through a new hull shape called mono-maran, featuring a monohull shape in the bow area that widens to mimic a catamaran shape toward the back. The result is a shape that helps boost fuel efficiency under power. Most importantly, stability and comfort are greatly improved whether underway or at anchor.
